chunks: There have been many dispensations before you; so travel in the land and see what befell those who denied the truth.

key_terms.سُنَنٌ: Dispensations or paths of previous nations

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about observing the fate of previous nations?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'takhalluf' (the succession of nations), urging believers to analyze the rise and fall of past civilizations as a sign of divine justice. It emphasizes that historical remnants serve as empirical evidence for the truth of prophethood, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on learning from the consequences of the 'Mukadhdhibeen' (those who denied the truth).
